activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix Using the Cofactor Method

feedback.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]$ if its determinant is $-4.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we want the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{31}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{31} & =(-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =15-(-1) \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{13}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{31}=\frac{1}{-4}\cdot 16=-4.\end{aligned}
$$
